title: Deuteronomy Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 31.

questions.question: How old did Moses say he was on the day he spoke to Israel?
options: 120 years old
100 years old
80 years old
60 years old
questions.correctAnswer: 120 years old
questions.explanation: Moses declared he was one hundred and twenty years old this day (Deuteronomy 31:2).

questions.question: Who did Moses say would go before Israel and destroy the nations?
options: The LORD thy God
Moses himself
Joshua
The priests
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD thy God
questions.explanation: Moses said the LORD thy God will go over before thee and destroy these nations (Deuteronomy 31:3).

questions.question: According to Moses, who will lead the Israelites into the land promised to their fathers?
options: Joshua
Aaron
Moses
Caleb
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua
questions.explanation: Moses said Joshua shall go over before thee, as the LORD hath said (Deuteronomy 31:3).

questions.question: What example did Moses give of how the LORD would deal with the nations before Israel?
options: As He did to Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites
As He did to Egypt
As He did to Babylon
As He did to the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: As He did to Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites
questions.explanation: The LORD shall do unto them as He did to Sihon and Og (Deuteronomy 31:4).

questions.question: Who did Moses say would give the nations into the Israelites' hands?
options: The LORD
Joshua
The priests
The elders
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The LORD shall give them up before your face, so you may do according to His commandments (Deuteronomy 31:5).

questions.question: What command did Moses give Israel regarding courage and fear?
options: Be strong and of a good courage; fear not
Hide and wait silently
Fear greatly and prepare for battle
Seek peace at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and of a good courage; fear not
questions.explanation: Moses commanded to be strong and courageous and not to fear, for the LORD goes with them (Deuteronomy 31:6).

questions.question: Who did Moses call to encourage in front of all Israel?
options: Joshua
Aaron
Caleb
Eleazar
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua
questions.explanation: Moses called Joshua and encouraged him before all Israel (Deuteronomy 31:7).

questions.question: What did Moses say about the LORD’s presence with Joshua?
options: He will be with you; He will not fail nor forsake you
He will leave you to lead alone
He will appear only in dreams
He will send prophets to guide you
questions.correctAnswer: He will be with you; He will not fail nor forsake you
questions.explanation: Moses assured Joshua that the LORD will be with him and not fail nor forsake him (Deuteronomy 31:8).

questions.question: To whom did Moses deliver the law he wrote?
options: The priests, sons of Levi, and all the elders of Israel
The Levites only
Joshua alone
All Israel without distinction
questions.correctAnswer: The priests, sons of Levi, and all the elders of Israel
questions.explanation: Moses wrote the law and delivered it to the priests, sons of Levi, and all the elders of Israel (Deuteronomy 31:9).

questions.question: When did Moses command the law to be read before Israel?
options: At the end of every seven years during the feast of tabernacles
Every Sabbath day
On the Day of Atonement
At the beginning of every year
questions.correctAnswer: At the end of every seven years during the feast of tabernacles
questions.explanation: Moses commanded reading the law every seven years in the solemnity of the year of release at the feast of tabernacles (Deuteronomy 31:10-11).

questions.question: Who did Moses command to be gathered to hear the law read?
options: Men, women, children, and strangers within the gates
Only men over 20 years old
Priests and Levites only
The elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Men, women, children, and strangers within the gates
questions.explanation: Moses instructed to gather all people including men, women, children, and strangers to hear and learn (Deuteronomy 31:12).

questions.question: True or False: Moses said he would lead the Israelites across the Jordan River.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Moses said the LORD told him he shall not go over this Jordan (Deuteronomy 31:2).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD appeared in a pillar of cloud over the tabernacle door when Moses and Joshua presented themselves.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The LORD appeared as a pillar of cloud over the door of the tabernacle (Deuteronomy 31:15).

questions.question: True or False: Moses was commanded to gather only the men of Israel to hear the law every seven years.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Moses commanded to gather men, women, children, and strangers, not only men (Deuteronomy 31:12).

questions.question: True or False: Moses told Joshua to be strong and courageous because he would bring Israel into the land promised by God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Moses encouraged Joshua to be strong and courageous as he would lead Israel to the promised land (Deuteronomy 31:7, 31:23).

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 31:11, when is the law to be read before all Israel?
options: At the end of every seven years during the feast of tabernacles
Every Sabbath day
During the Passover feast every year
On the first day of the new year
questions.correctAnswer: At the end of every seven years during the feast of tabernacles
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:10-11 instruct that at the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release and the feast of tabernacles, the law shall be read before all Israel in their hearing to ensure they learn and fear the LORD.

questions.question: Who are to be gathered to hear the reading of the law according to Deuteronomy 31:12?
options: Only the men and priests
Men, women, children, and strangers within the gates
Only the elders and officers
Only the Levites and priests
questions.correctAnswer: Men, women, children, and strangers within the gates
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:12 commands gathering the entire community—men, women, children, and strangers within the gates—so that all may hear, learn, and fear the LORD, showing inclusiveness in obedience.

questions.question: What is the purpose of teaching the children the law as stated in Deuteronomy 31:13?
options: So they may become priests
So they may fear the LORD as long as they live in the land
So they can lead the people after Moses
So they will know the history of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: So they may fear the LORD as long as they live in the land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:13 explains that children who have not known anything must hear and learn to fear the LORD God as a lifelong principle, especially as they live in the land God gives them.

questions.question: What does God reveal to Moses about the future behavior of the people in Deuteronomy 31:16?
options: They will remain faithful to His covenant forever
They will rise up and worship the gods of the strangers and forsake God
They will conquer all their enemies without fail
They will immediately obey Joshua's leadership
questions.correctAnswer: They will rise up and worship the gods of the strangers and forsake God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:16 reveals God's knowledge that after Moses dies, the people will turn to other gods and break His covenant, highlighting human tendency towards unfaithfulness despite God's faithfulness.

questions.question: What consequence does God say will happen when the people forsake Him according to Deuteronomy 31:17?
options: God will bless them with prosperity
God will forsake them and many evils will befall them
God will give them a new land
God will send angels to protect them
questions.correctAnswer: God will forsake them and many evils will befall them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:17 explains that God's anger will be kindled, He will forsake the people, hide His face, and many evils and troubles will come upon them as a consequence of their unfaithfulness.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 31:18, how will God respond to the evils wrought by the people turning to other gods?
options: He will forgive immediately
He will hide His face from them
He will send them prophets
He will increase their blessings
questions.correctAnswer: He will hide His face from them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:18 states that God will hide His face in response to all the evils caused by the people's turning to other gods, emphasizing the serious consequence of idolatry.

questions.question: What did God command Moses to do in Deuteronomy 31:19 to help remind Israel of their covenant obligations?
options: Write a song and teach it to the children of Israel
Build a new tabernacle
Offer sacrifices daily
Appoint more priests
questions.correctAnswer: Write a song and teach it to the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:19 commands Moses to write a song and teach it to the children of Israel so that the song may serve as a witness against them if they break the covenant, showing a practical method to preserve memory and obedience.

questions.question: Based on Deuteronomy 31:20, what will happen after Israel has been brought into the land flowing with milk and honey and become prosperous?
options: They will remain faithful to God forever
They will turn to other gods and break the covenant
They will immediately build a temple
They will appoint Joshua as king
questions.correctAnswer: They will turn to other gods and break the covenant
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:20 warns that after enjoying prosperity in the promised land, Israel will become complacent, turn to other gods, serve them, and break the covenant, demonstrating the danger of spiritual complacency.

questions.question: What is the connection between Deuteronomy 31:12 and 31:13 regarding teaching the law to the people?
options: Verse 12 focuses on adults, while verse 13 focuses on strangers
Verse 12 commands gathering all people to hear the law, and verse 13 explains the purpose is for children to learn to fear God
Verse 12 is about building the tabernacle, and verse 13 is about Joshua's leadership
Verse 12 talks about sacrifices, and verse 13 about festivals
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 12 commands gathering all people to hear the law, and verse 13 explains the purpose is for children to learn to fear God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:12 commands gathering men, women, children, and strangers to hear the law, while verse 13 states the purpose is so that the children who do not know the law will learn to fear the LORD, linking communal hearing with lifelong reverence.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 31:14-15, what significant event happens when Moses and Joshua present themselves in the tabernacle?
options: The LORD appears in a pillar of cloud over the door of the tabernacle
Moses is crowned king
Joshua writes the law
The people build an altar
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD appears in a pillar of cloud over the door of the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:14-15 describes how the LORD appears to Moses and Joshua in the tabernacle as a pillar of cloud standing over its door, signifying God's presence and approval as Joshua is charged with leadership.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 31:21 teach about the role of the song Moses wrote?
options: It is to be sung every Sabbath
It will testify against Israel when evils befall them
It is a prayer for rain
It appoints Joshua as leader
questions.correctAnswer: It will testify against Israel when evils befall them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:21 explains that the song Moses wrote will serve as a witness against Israel during times of trouble because it contains a testimony of their rebellion and God's warnings, ensuring the memory of God's covenant.

questions.question: What charge does Moses give to Joshua in Deuteronomy 31:23?
options: To build a temple in the promised land
To be strong and courageous to bring Israel into the land God promised
To write the law again
To gather the elders for a council
questions.correctAnswer: To be strong and courageous to bring Israel into the land God promised
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:23 records Moses charging Joshua to be strong and courageous as he leads the children of Israel into the land God swore to give them, assuring Joshua of God's presence.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 31:26 instruct regarding the book of the law Moses wrote?
options: To be hidden in the tabernacle
To be placed beside the ark of the covenant as a witness
To be given to the priests only
To be destroyed after reading
questions.correctAnswer: To be placed beside the ark of the covenant as a witness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:26 commands the Levites to put the book of the law beside the ark of the covenant so it may serve as a witness against the people, symbolizing God’s covenant and law standing with them.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 31:27 reveals that Moses knew the people would be more rebellious after his death.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:27 explicitly states Moses' awareness of Israel's rebellion during his life and predicts that they will be even more rebellious after his death, highlighting the challenge of maintaining faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 31:28-29, Moses calls heaven and earth to record against Israel because he anticipates their future faithfulness.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:28-29 shows Moses calling heaven and earth to witness Israel's future corruption and turning away from God's commandments, not their faithfulness, emphasizing accountability.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 31.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the song Moses wrote, according to Deuteronomy 31?
options: To celebrate Israel’s victory over their enemies
To serve as a witness against the children of Israel
To teach the history of Israel's journey in the wilderness
To praise the priests who carried the ark
questions.correctAnswer: To serve as a witness against the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:19 explains that the song was written to be a witness against the children of Israel. This theme is echoed in Hosea 12:10, where God also uses prophetic words as a witness against Israel.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 31, what does God predict will happen to Israel after Moses dies?
options: They will enter the Promised Land without any trouble
They will remain faithful to God's covenant
They will go whoring after the gods of the strangers and break the covenant
They will build a temple as a sign of their devotion
questions.correctAnswer: They will go whoring after the gods of the strangers and break the covenant
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:16 foretells that Israel will abandon God and worship other gods after Moses dies, breaking the covenant. This theme is further developed in Judges 2:19, where Israel's unfaithfulness after Joshua's death is described.

questions.question: Who did Moses charge to carry the book of the law and place it beside the ark of the covenant?
options: The elders of Israel
The priests, the sons of Levi
The Levites who bore the ark
Joshua son of Nun
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites who bore the ark
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:25-26 commands the Levites who bore the ark to take the book of the law and place it beside the ark as a witness. This connects with the role of the Levites as caretakers of the sacred objects in Numbers 4.

questions.question: What specific command does Moses give about the reading of the law every seven years?
options: It should be read privately by the priests
It should be read only to the men of Israel
It should be read publicly to all Israel including strangers
It should be written on stone tablets
questions.correctAnswer: It should be read publicly to all Israel including strangers
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:10-12 commands that every seven years, during the Feast of Tabernacles, the law must be read before all Israel, including men, women, children, and strangers, so all may hear and learn. This public reading is echoed in Nehemiah 8:2-3.

questions.question: What does God promise Joshua as he is charged to lead Israel into the Promised Land?
options: That he will be rich and prosperous
That he will have many children
That the LORD will be with him and will not forsake him
That no enemies will oppose him
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD will be with him and will not forsake him
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:23 reveals God's promise to Joshua to be strong and courageous because God will be with him and not forsake him. This promise is reaffirmed in Joshua 1:5-9.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'stiff neck' in Deuteronomy 31:27 symbolize in the context of Israel's behavior?
options: Their physical strength
Their stubbornness and rebelliousness
Their ability to lead
Their wisdom and understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Their stubbornness and rebelliousness
questions.explanation: The phrase 'stiff neck' in Deuteronomy 31:27 symbolizes Israel's stubborn and rebellious attitude toward God, a common Hebrew idiom for obstinacy, as also seen in Exodus 32:9.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 31, what is the role of the elders and officers called to Moses before his death?
options: To assist Joshua in battle
To hear Moses' final words and be witnesses
To take care of the ark of the covenant
To lead the sacrificial offerings
questions.correctAnswer: To hear Moses' final words and be witnesses
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:28 says Moses called the elders and officers to hear his words and to have heaven and earth called as witnesses against them. This public witnessing is a legal and covenantal practice found in Deuteronomy 4:26.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Deuteronomy 31:21-22 regarding the song Moses wrote?
options: Chiasmus
Inclusio
Parallelism
Typology
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:21-22 uses inclusio by introducing the song as a witness (v.21) and then stating Moses wrote and taught it the same day (v.22), framing the message with emphasis. This framing device highlights the importance of the song as a covenant witness, similar to the inclusio in Psalm 8.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was allowed by the LORD to cross over the Jordan River into the Promised Land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:2 states that the LORD told Moses he would not cross over the Jordan, indicating he was not permitted to enter the Promised Land.

questions.question: True or False: Moses encouraged Joshua to be strong and courageous multiple times because Joshua would lead Israel into the land God promised to their fathers.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:7, 8, and 23 all show Moses and God encouraging Joshua to be strong and courageous to lead Israel into the promised land, emphasizing the importance of Joshua’s role.

questions.question: Which other biblical book strongly echoes the theme of Israel's rebellion and God's anger as foretold in Deuteronomy 31:16-17?
options: Exodus
Judges
Psalms
Proverbs
questions.correctAnswer: Judges
questions.explanation: The book of Judges repeatedly shows Israel turning away from God after Joshua's death, provoking God's anger, which directly echoes the warning in Deuteronomy 31:16-17.

questions.question: What is the significance of placing the book of the law beside the ark of the covenant, as commanded in Deuteronomy 31:26?
options: It symbolizes the law's authority and witness over Israel
It was to protect the book from damage
It allowed the priests to read it daily
It was a sign of God’s absence
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the law's authority and witness over Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:26 states the book of the law is put by the ark as a witness against Israel, symbolizing the binding authority of God's covenant, similar to covenant treaties in the ancient Near East.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 31 foreshadow New Testament themes about God's faithfulness despite human rebellion?
options: By promising a Messiah who will forgive sins
By emphasizing God's presence even when Israel fails
By predicting the destruction of the temple
By foretelling the coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: By emphasizing God's presence even when Israel fails
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:6 and 8 emphasize that God will not forsake His people despite their failures, a theme echoed in Hebrews 13:5 and Romans 11:29 about God's unchanging faithfulness.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the phrase translated 'Be strong and of a good courage' (Deuteronomy 31:6), and why is it significant?
options: 'Chazaq' meaning strong and 'Amats' meaning steadfast, signifying inner strength and perseverance
'Shalom' meaning peace and 'Emet' meaning truth, signifying harmony and faithfulness
'Chesed' meaning mercy and 'Rachamim' meaning compassion, signifying God’s love
'Ruach' meaning spirit and 'Neshamah' meaning breath, signifying life and inspiration
questions.correctAnswer: 'Chazaq' meaning strong and 'Amats' meaning steadfast, signifying inner strength and perseverance
questions.explanation: The Hebrew words 'Chazaq' (strong) and 'Amats' (steadfast) in Deuteronomy 31:6 call Joshua and Israel to inner strength and courage facing challenges, emphasizing perseverance in faith, as also seen in Joshua 1:9.

questions.question: What historical or cultural significance does the Feast of Tabernacles have in the context of the law reading commanded in Deuteronomy 31:10-11?
options: It commemorates the giving of the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai
It celebrates the harvest and Israel’s wilderness journey
It marks the start of the new year
It honors the kings of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It celebrates the harvest and Israel’s wilderness journey
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:10-11 commands the law to be read during the Feast of Tabernacles, which culturally commemorates the harvest and Israel’s wilderness sojourn, reminding them of God’s provision and covenant.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily emphasized in God's promise to Joshua in Deuteronomy 31:8?
options: God's omnipresence and faithfulness
God's wrath and judgment
God's mercy and forgiveness
God's omniscience
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipresence and faithfulness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 31:8 highlights that the LORD 'doth go before thee; he will be with thee, he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee,' which reveals God's omnipresence and faithfulness to His people.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 31:6, what reason is given for Israel to 'be strong and of a good courage'?
options: Because Moses will lead them across Jordan
Because the LORD thy God goes with thee and will not forsake thee
Because the land is already conquered
Because the enemy will surrender without a fight
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD thy God goes with thee and will not forsake thee
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states that the people should be strong and courageous because the LORD their God goes with them and will neither fail nor forsake them, emphasizing God's sustaining presence.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine judgment and covenant faithfulness is taught in Deuteronomy 31:16-18?
options: That God will forgive all sins without consequences
That God will hide His face and bring judgment when Israel breaks the covenant by idolatry
That Israel will never turn away from God
That God will always intervene to save Israel regardless of their actions
questions.correctAnswer: That God will hide His face and bring judgment when Israel breaks the covenant by idolatry
questions.explanation: These verses teach that if Israel forsakes God and breaks his covenant to worship other gods, God’s anger will kindle, He will hide His face, and judgment will come, demonstrating the seriousness of covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does the instruction in Deuteronomy 31:9-13 contribute to the doctrine of covenant education and communal responsibility?
options: It establishes that only priests should know the law
It commands the public reading of the law to all men, women, children, and foreigners every seven years
It allows selective teaching of the law only to adult males
It mandates silent meditation on the law without communal involvement
questions.correctAnswer: It commands the public reading of the law to all men, women, children, and foreigners every seven years
questions.explanation: Verses 9-13 emphasize communal responsibility to teach the law openly so that everyone, including children and strangers, may learn to fear the LORD and obey, reinforcing covenant education as a corporate and intergenerational duty.

questions.question: What theological significance does Moses’ age and inability to cross the Jordan have in Deuteronomy 31:2?
options: It shows human limitation and the transition of leadership by God's sovereign will
It indicates Moses’ failure as a leader
It proves that the Israelites will never enter the promised land
It shows that God abandoned Moses
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human limitation and the transition of leadership by God's sovereign will
questions.explanation: Moses being 120 years old and unable to cross the Jordan (verse 2) demonstrates human frailty and God's sovereign plan to transition leadership to Joshua, emphasizing divine providence in salvation history.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 31:26 teach about the role of the Law in Israel's covenant relationship with God?
options: The Law is to be hidden from the people
The Law is placed beside the ark as a witness against Israel
The Law is optional for most Israelites
The Law was to be destroyed after Moses’ death
questions.correctAnswer: The Law is placed beside the ark as a witness against Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 26 commands placing the book of the law beside the ark of the covenant, symbolizing that the Law stands as a witness against Israel's obedience or disobedience in their covenant relationship with God.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about God's providence and human responsibility is taught by Deuteronomy 31:23 and Deuteronomy 31:6?
options: God is passive; humans must achieve salvation alone
God’s presence ensures success, but humans must be strong and courageous to fulfill His promises
God will automatically save Israel regardless of their courage
Human effort is irrelevant because God alone acts
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence ensures success, but humans must be strong and courageous to fulfill His promises
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize God's presence with Joshua and Israel (31:23, 31:6) and simultaneously call for human strength and courage to inherit the land, showing the synergy of divine providence and human responsibility.

questions.question: How does Moses’ command in Deuteronomy 31:28 reflect the seriousness of covenant accountability before God?
options: It calls only the priests for counsel
It summons all elders and officers to hear Moses’ words, calling heaven and earth as witnesses against Israel
It instructs secret meetings away from the people
It avoids any formal record of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It summons all elders and officers to hear Moses’ words, calling heaven and earth as witnesses against Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 28 demonstrates covenant accountability by gathering leaders to hear Moses’ warnings and invoking heaven and earth as witnesses, underscoring the solemn and universal nature of the covenant obligations.

questions.question: What does the prophecy in Deuteronomy 31:29 reveal about human nature and covenant failure?
options: Humans will remain perfectly faithful
Humans have a tendency to corrupt themselves and turn away from God's commands, provoking His anger
Humans will never provoke God
Humans are incapable of sin
questions.correctAnswer: Humans have a tendency to corrupt themselves and turn away from God's commands, provoking His anger
questions.explanation: Verse 29 predicts Israel’s future corruption and departure from God's commands, reflecting the doctrine of human sinfulness and covenant failure that provokes divine wrath.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 31:19-21 illustrate the function of the song Moses was commanded to write?
options: The song is purely celebratory with no legal significance
The song serves as a witness and testimony against Israel when they forsake God
The song is meant to entertain the people
The song replaces the written law
questions.correctAnswer: The song serves as a witness and testimony against Israel when they forsake God
questions.explanation: These verses explain that the song is a witness against Israel’s future rebellion, intended to remind and testify against them if they break God's covenant.

questions.question: What redemptive narrative arc is evident in Deuteronomy 31:3-5 regarding God’s promise and action toward the nations before Israel?
options: God will abandon Israel to the nations
God will go before Israel, destroy the nations, and give Israel possession of the land as fulfillment of His covenant promises
Israel will conquer the nations through their own power
The nations will convert Israel to idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: God will go before Israel, destroy the nations, and give Israel possession of the land as fulfillment of His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Verses 3-5 reveal God’s promise to lead Israel, defeat the nations, and grant them the land, continuing the covenant narrative of promise, deliverance, and possession central to redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's covenant justice and mercy can be drawn from Deuteronomy 31:17 and 31:18?
options: God will ignore sin and show no judgment
God will execute just judgment by hiding His face due to Israel's sins but His actions aim to bring them to repentance
God's mercy cancels all consequences
God's justice is arbitrary
questions.correctAnswer: God will execute just judgment by hiding His face due to Israel's sins but His actions aim to bring them to repentance
questions.explanation: These verses describe God's anger and hidden face as consequences of Israel’s sin, highlighting His just judgment while implying His ultimate desire for their return (cf. 2 Chronicles 7:14).

questions.question: How does the charge given to Joshua in Deuteronomy 31:7 and 31:23 relate to the doctrine of divine commissioning?
options: It shows Joshua acting independently from God
It reflects God's sovereign commissioning of a leader to fulfill His promises and lead His people
It is a private matter with no public aspect
It implies Joshua's leadership is temporary and insignificant
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God's sovereign commissioning of a leader to fulfill His promises and lead His people
questions.explanation: Both verses show Moses publicly charging Joshua to be strong and courageous to lead Israel into the promised land, demonstrating divine commissioning as God’s method for fulfilling His covenant promises.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Deuteronomy 31:27-29 provide to skeptics who claim that the Mosaic Law was too harsh and contradictory to God's love?
options: It reveals that God's law is irrelevant
It explains that God's law includes warnings of judgment due to human rebellion, demonstrating His holiness and justice alongside His love
It suggests that God does not care about human sin
It denies any accountability for sin
questions.correctAnswer: It explains that God's law includes warnings of judgment due to human rebellion, demonstrating His holiness and justice alongside His love
questions.explanation: Verses 27-29 acknowledge Israel's rebellion and warn of future judgment, showing that God's law is just and holy, balancing His love with righteous accountability, countering claims of harshness without justice.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 31:15 reveal about God's presence with Israel during their wilderness journey?
options: God abandoned Israel in the wilderness
God appeared visibly in a pillar of cloud over the tabernacle
God was invisible and distant
God’s presence was only in the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: God appeared visibly in a pillar of cloud over the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Verse 15 describes the LORD appearing as a pillar of cloud over the tabernacle door, demonstrating God's tangible and guiding presence with Israel during their journey.
